column1: In Paris, urban farmers are trying a soil-free approach to agriculture that uses less space and fewer resources.
column2: 在巴黎，城市农户正在尝试一种无土栽培方式，所需空间更小、资源也更少。

column1: Could it help cities face the threats to our food supplies?
column2: 这种方法能帮助城市应对食物供应面临的威胁吗？

column1: On top of a striking new exhibition hall in southern Paris, the world’s largest urban rooftop farm has started to bear fruit.
column2: 巴黎南部一座引人注目的新展览馆楼顶上，全球最大的城市屋顶农场已开始结出果实。
column7: bear fruit|结出果实；初见成效

column1: Strawberries that are small, intensely flavoured and resplendently red sprout abundantly from large plastic tubes.
column2: 一颗颗草莓从粗大的塑料管中密密地长出来，个头虽小，却滋味浓郁，红得鲜亮。

column1: Peer inside and you see the tubes are completely hollow, the roots of dozens of strawberry plants dangling down inside them.
column2: 往里一瞧，就会发现管子完全是空心的，几十株草莓的根垂在里面。

column1: From identical vertical tubes nearby burst row upon row of lettuces; near those are aromatic herbs, such as basil, sage and peppermint.
column2: 旁边相同的竖管里，一排排生菜簇拥而出；生菜近旁长着罗勒、鼠尾草和胡椒薄荷等香草。
column5: row upon row of|一排又一排的

column1: Opposite, in narrow, horizontal trays packed not with soil but with coconut fibre, grow cherry tomatoes, shiny aubergines and brightly coloured chards.
column2: 对面狭长的水平种植槽里装满了椰子纤维，没有泥土。里面长着樱桃番茄、油亮的茄子和色彩鲜艳的叶用甜菜。

column1: Pascal Hardy, an engineer and sustainable development consultant, began experimenting with vertical farming and aeroponic growing towers — as the soil-free plastic tubes are known — on his Paris apartment block roof five years ago.
column2: 帕斯卡尔·阿尔迪是一名工程师兼可持续发展顾问。五年前，他开始在自己所住的巴黎公寓楼顶试验垂直农业，使用的气雾栽培塔就是这些无土塑料管。
column8: aeroponic growing towers|n. 气雾栽培塔

column1: The urban rooftop space above the exhibition hall is somewhat bigger: 14,000 square metres and almost exactly the size of a couple of football pitches.
column2: 展览馆顶上的这块城市空间要大些，有1.4万平方米，几乎正好相当于两个足球场。

column1: Already, the team of young urban farmers who tend it have picked, in one day, 3,000 lettuces and 150 punnets of strawberries.
column2: 照料农场的这群年轻城市农户，已经有过一天采下3000棵生菜和150小盒草莓的收成。
column7: punnets|n. 装软质水果的小盒或小篮

column1: When the remaining two thirds of the vast open area are in production, 20 staff will harvest up to 1,000 kg of perhaps 35 different varieties of fruit and vegetables, every day.
column2: 等这片开阔场地其余三分之二也投入生产，20名员工每天最多可采收1000公斤果蔬，品种或许有35种。

column1: ‘We’re not ever, obviously, going to feed the whole city this way,’ cautions Hardy.
column2: 阿尔迪提醒说：“显然，我们永远无法靠这种方式养活整座城市的人。”

column1: ‘In the urban environment you’re working with very significant practical constraints, clearly, on what you can do and where.
column2: “在城市环境中，能做什么、在哪里做，显然都受到很大的现实限制。

column1: But if enough unused space can be developed like this, there’s no reason why you shouldn’t eventually target maybe between 5% and 10% of consumption.’
column2: 不过，如果能像这样把足够多的闲置空间开发出来，最终把目标定在满足消费量的5%到10%左右，也未尝不可。”
column5: there’s no reason why|没有理由不……

column1: Perhaps most significantly, however, this is a real-life showcase for the work of Hardy’s flourishing urban agriculture consultancy, Agripolis, which is currently fielding enquiries from around the world to design, build and equip a new breed of soil-free inner-city farm.
column2: 不过，或许最重要的是，这里为阿尔迪生意兴隆的城市农业咨询公司Agripolis提供了一个展示成果的现实范例。该公司目前正接洽来自世界各地的咨询，为新型市区无土农场提供设计、建设和设备配置服务。
column4: real-life showcase|n. 展示成果的现实范例

column1: ‘The method’s advantages are many,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“这种方法有很多优点。”

column1: ‘First, I don’t much like the fact that most of the fruit and vegetables we eat have been treated with something like 17 different pesticides, or that the intensive farming techniques that produced them are such huge generators of greenhouse gases.
column2: “首先，我们吃的大部分果蔬都用过大约17种不同的农药，我对这一点很不以为然；同样让我不喜欢的是，生产这些果蔬的集约化耕作方式会产生大量温室气体。

column1: I don’t much like the fact, either, that they’ve travelled an average of 2,000 refrigerated kilometres to my plate, that their quality is so poor, because the varieties are selected for their capacity to withstand such substantial journeys, or that 80% of the price I pay goes to wholesalers and transport companies, not the producers.’
column2: 我同样不喜欢的是，这些果蔬要经过平均2000公里的冷藏运输才到我的餐桌上；它们的品质也很差，因为选用品种看重的是能否经受这么长的旅程；而我付的钱有80%进了批发商和运输公司的口袋，没有落到生产者手里。”

column1: Produce grown using this soil-free method, on the other hand — which relies solely on a small quantity of water, enriched with organic nutrients, pumped around a closed circuit of pipes, towers and trays — is ‘produced up here, and sold locally, just down there.
column2: 相比之下，用这种无土方法种出来的农产品，只需少量添加了有机养分的水，通过管道、栽培塔和种植槽构成的封闭系统循环输送，便可“在楼顶生产，就在下面的当地出售。
column8: closed circuit|n. 封闭循环系统

column1: It barely travels at all,’ Hardy says.
column2: 几乎一点路都不用走就能送到，”阿尔迪说。

column1: ‘You can select crop varieties for their flavour, not their resistance to the transport and storage chain, and you can pick them when they’re really at their best, and not before.’
column2: “你选种时可以看风味，用不着考虑它们能不能经得起一路运输和储存；还可以等到果蔬真正达到最佳状态时才采摘，不用提前。”
column10: at their best|处于最佳状态

column1: No soil is exhausted, and the water that gently showers the plants’ roots every 12 minutes is recycled, so the method uses 90% less water than a classic intensive farm for the same yield.
column2: 土壤肥力不会被耗尽；每隔12分钟轻轻喷洒在植株根部的水会回收再用，因此在产量相同的情况下，这种方法比传统集约化农场少用90%的水。

column1: Urban farming is not, of course, a new phenomenon.
column2: 当然，城市农业并不是一种新现象。

column1: Inner-city agriculture is booming from Shanghai to Detroit and Tokyo to Bangkok.
column2: 从上海到底特律，从东京到曼谷，市区农业正蓬勃发展。

column1: Strawberries are being grown in disused shipping containers, mushrooms in underground carparks.
column2: 闲置的集装箱被用来种草莓，地下停车场则用来种蘑菇。

column1: Aeroponic farming, he says, is ‘virtuous’.
column2: 他说，气雾栽培是种“良性的”耕作方式。

column1: The equipment weighs little, can be installed on almost any flat surface and is cheap to buy: roughly €100 to €150 per square metre.
column2: 设备轻巧，几乎任何平坦表面都能安装，购买的成本也低，约每平方米100至150欧元。

column1: It is cheap to run, too, consuming a tiny fraction of the electricity used by some techniques.
column2: 运行成本也很低，耗电量只是某些其他技术的一小部分。
column5: a tiny fraction of|……的极小一部分

column1: Produce grown this way typically sells at prices that, while generally higher than those of classic intensive agriculture, are lower than soil-based organic growers.
column2: 这样种出来的农产品，售价通常比传统集约农业产品高，却低于在土壤中有机栽培的农产品。
column8: organic growers|n. 有机农产品种植者

column1: There are limits to what farmers can grow this way, of course, and much of the produce is suited to the summer months.
column2: 当然，用这种方式能种的品种有限，而且很多农产品都更适宜在夏季种植。

column1: ‘Root vegetables we cannot do, at least not yet,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“根菜类我们种不了，至少目前还不行。”

column1: ‘Radishes are OK, but carrots, potatoes, that kind of thing — the roots are simply too long.
column2: “小萝卜可以，但胡萝卜、马铃薯这类就不行了——它们的根实在太长。

column1: Fruit trees are obviously not an option.
column2: 果树显然也不在可选之列。
column5: not an option|不在可选之列

column1: And beans tend to take up a lot of space for not much return.’
column2: 而豆类往往很占地方，收成却不多。”

column1: Nevertheless, urban farming of the kind being practised in Paris is one part of a bigger and fast-changing picture that is bringing food production closer to our lives.
column2: 尽管如此，巴黎正在实践的这类城市农业，仍是一个更宏大且正在迅速变化的图景中的一部分。它正让食物生产更贴近我们的生活。
